content: Cefprozil is a cephalosporin antibiotic used to treat a variety of bacterial infections. It is effective only against bacterial infections and will not work for viral infections such as the common cold or flu. This medication is typically taken orally once or twice daily, as directed by your doctor. If stomach upset occurs, it can be taken with food. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition and response to treatment. For optimal results, take this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals and complete the full prescribed course, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Common side effects may include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, stomach pain, or dizziness. While rare, this medication may cause a severe intestinal condition due to the bacteria Clostridium difficile (C. difficile), which can occur during treatment or weeks to months after stopping the medication. Prolonged or repeated use of cefprozil may lead to oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare but possible. If you experience any unusual or severe symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. Before taking cefprozil, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, penicillins, other cephalosporin antibiotics (e.g., cephalexin), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Cefprozil may cause dizziness, and consuming alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can worsen this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages while taking this medication. Cefprozil may interfere with the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed, as it passes into breast milk. Discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor if you are breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Cefprozil may interfere with certain lab tests, such as diabetic urine tests or blood glucose tests, potentially causing false results. If someone overdoses and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Consult your pharmacist or local waste disposal company for proper disposal instructions. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
